newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to continue probe into aid to Danish shipyards.
newsitem.headline: EU to continue probe into aid to Danish shipyards.

text.p: The European Commission will complete its probe into Danish shipbuilding aid, despite a Danish industry ministry report saying EU aid ceilings had not been exceeded, a Commission source said on Thursday.
The source said the Commission received a letter from Danish Industry Minister Mimi Jacobsen with the report earlier on Thursday.
"We are going to analyse the report," he told reporters.

He noted that the Commission had opened proceedings in July and that there was a September 16 deadline for comments from the Danish government and competitors. There had been no comments from competitors so far, he said.
On Wednesday, Jacobsen presented the ministry report which concluded that her ministry's administration of shipbuilding aid in the period 1986-95 was in accordance with EU rules.
Jacobsen said she was dropping a planned legal probe into state shipbuilding aid, rejecting the findings of a critical independent study accusing the government of illegalities.

In July, the Commission announced it was starting a probe to investigate Danish shipbuilding aid after seeing the study, fearing that Denmark's ship subsidies might have exceeded EU limits in the period.

On the basis of the study, the Commission at the time said there were indications that in 65 cases vessels were financed during the period on the basis of an inflated price level, "which has created a risk that the state aid ceiling was exceeded".

But Jacobsen said her ministry had studied 308 cases of aid granted to Danish shipbuilding yards in the period 1986-1995 and found that the report's critical stance was unfounded and full of errors and misinterpretations of EU rules.

The study, commissioned by the ministry and carried out by international accountancy firm Coopers & Lybrand, criticised changing Danish governments for subsidising the sector to the tune of four billion crowns ($697 million) between 1986-1995.
